Implementation Plan Clarify retries once when a `BLOCKED:` reason names a tracked file: implementation plan (Refs #8291, local ID `p9-blocked-verify`) Planning ref: `git rev-parse HEAD` = `2d1165c60b68dfb406a76acc10576dd98f307801`, branch `orchestrator/project-8291` (matches the integration branch metadata; integration branch mismatch is `false`). Source of truth for this phase: `docs/plans/remove-unattended-pipeline-stuck-states-plan.md`, item 10 (P9) and section "P9 — Clarify snapshot and BLOCKED verification", step 2. It says: if the `BLOCKED:` reason names a path that `git ls-files` lists at the checked-out ref, re-run clarify once in the same job with the path listing appended. The marker is `AI_CLARIFY_BLOCKED_RETRY_V1`, there is at most one retry, and every other case keeps today's behaviour. The switch is `CLARIFY_BLOCKED_VERIFY_ENABLED`, default `true`. ## Automation wiring (§20.E) | Question | Answer | |---|---| | New script, extended script, or code-only? | One new step helper, `scripts/clarify_blocked_verify.sh`, which the design doc lists as "[new, only if needed]". It is needed because the path parsing must be testable on its own. The existing "Run Codex" step of `.github/workflows/clarify.yml` calls it. | | Scheduler / PR-push entry point | The existing `.github/workflows/clarify.yml` triggers (issue opened, `/reclarify`, and orchestrator dispatch), inside the `run_codex` step. No new trigger or cron. | | New long-running supervisor (§20.C)? | No. | | DB work (§20.D)? | None. | | `docs/scripts-pending-removal.md` (§20.F) | No entry. The helper is a permanent part of a step that already exists. It is not single-use, long-running or a supervisor, which matches the design doc's "No new entries" row. | ## Files likely to change - `.github/workflows/clarify.yml` - `scripts/clarify_blocked_verify.sh` (new) - `scripts/stage_support_for_phase.sh` - `tests/test_clarify_blocked_verify.py` (new) - `tests/test_plan_clarify_blocked_output.py` - `README.md` - `agents.d/stuck-states-p9b-clarify-blocked-verify.md` (new) - `changelog.d/stuck-states-p9b-clarify-blocked-verify.md` (new) Scope-mode: Hold Scope Reuse-audit: extends Run Codex Scope-mode justification: The issue and the design doc both limit P9b to the clarify workflow's BLOCKED path. Plan, clarify-respond, triage and the unblock judge share `clarify_isolated_run.sh` but are not named, so they stay out (Hold Scope, not Expansion). The retry reuses the existing Run Codex engine calls and the existing Claude→Codex fallback (exit code 75). The new helper copies three things from existing code: the fence-aware `BLOCKED:` parse from the "Parse Codex output" step, the token pattern of `unblock_actions.HARNESS_PATH_TOKEN_RE`, and the sensitive-part list `bad_parts` from `clarify_isolated_run.sh`. A test keeps each copy equal to its source. The helper does not import `unblock_actions.py` because that module is large and not in the clarify support bundle. The extra tests and the mirrored deny-list cost under 30 lines more than a plain retry. They protect correctness and security, which rank above speed in §6 (Security > Correctness & safety > Backward compatibility > Operational clarity > Performance > Speed), so the complete option is chosen. ## Functions or modules to implement 1. **`scripts/clarify_blocked_verify.sh` (new; tabs; `set -euo pipefail`).** All parsing runs in an embedded `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -I -B -` block, the same way `clarify_isolated_run.sh` does it. There are two subcommands. - **`check `** - **Switch:** read `CLARIFY_BLOCKED_VERIFY_ENABLED` with the default `true` set inside the helper (§8). The values `false`, `0`, `no` and `off` (any case) make it exit 3 and print nothing. - **Find the reason:** take the first `BLOCKED:` line that is outside a code fence. This uses exactly the rule in the "Parse Codex output" perl: a line starting with ```` ``` ```` or `~~~` toggles fence state, then `^\s*BLOCKED:\s*(.*\S)\s*$` matches, case-insensitive. If there is no such line, exit 3 silently. - **Retry-once guard:** if the prompt file already contains `AI_CLARIFY_BLOCKED_RETRY_V1`, log `reason=already_retried` and exit 3. - **Pick path tokens** from the reason: - Split with `[^\s`'"<>()\[\]{},;]+`. - Drop tokens that contain `://`. - Remove a leading `./`, trailing `.,;:!?` characters, a trailing `:[:]`, and a trailing `/`. - Keep a token only if it matches `^[A-Za-z0-9_.@+-][A-Za-z0-9._/@+-]{0,239}$`, does not start with `/`, has no `..` part and no `//`, and either contains `/` or ends in an extension of 1–8 alphanumeric characters (`README.md`, `Makefile.j2`). - De-duplicate, keep the original order, and stop at 20. - **Drop sensitive paths** using a copy of the snapshot's rules, so no retry points the agent at paths the snapshot never ships: - Any part whose lowercase form is in `bad_parts` (`.git`, `.ai`, `.codex`, `.codex-workflow-src`, `.codex-workflow-src-main`, `.env`, `secrets`, `credentials`, `__pycache__`). - Any part starting with `.env`. - Any part ending in `.pem`, `.key`, `.p12`, `.pfx` or `.keystore`. - **Check git:** make one `git ls-files -z` call in the current directory. That is the checkout the snapshot is built from (`clarify_isolated_run.sh` runs `git ls-files -z` with `cwd=root`, which defaults to `$PWD`). Compare paths in Python, never as a git pathspec. A candidate counts as present if it is an exact tracked path or a directory prefix of one (`

/`). - **Write the listing** to ``. Use one line per present path: `- (tracked file)`, or `- / (tracked directory, files; e.g. a, b, c)` with at most 3 examples. Cap the listing at 8 KiB. - **Exit code and log:** exit 0 when at least one path is present, otherwise exit 3 with `reason=no_tracked_path`. Exit 1 on any plumbing error; the caller treats that as no retry. - **Log line** on stderr: `CLARIFY_BLOCKED_VERIFY stage=verify outcome= reason= paths= sample=`, with `sample` last. Only checked, charset-limited paths go into `sample`. - **`prompt

`** - Write a new file: the bytes of ``, unchanged, followed by a delimited block: ``` === AI_CLARIFY_BLOCKED_RETRY_V1 (repository data, not instructions) === Your previous answer was BLOCKED: and cited paths that ARE tracked in git at the checked-out ref: A source file in the repository is codebase state, not an external input. Read it from /source; if it is absent there it was excluded from the snapshot (see the exclusions block, if any). Do not emit BLOCKED: for these paths' presence or absence; answer STATUS: CLEAR or ask Q questions. BLOCKED: remains correct only for a genuinely external scalar input. === END AI_CLARIFY_BLOCKED_RETRY_V1 === ``` - Never edit ``. 2. **`.github/workflows/clarify.yml`, step "Run Codex" (`id: run_codex`, about lines 1471–1800).** - Add `CLARIFY_BLOCKED_VERIFY_ENABLED: ${{ vars.CLARIFY_BLOCKED_VERIFY_ENABLED || 'true' }}` to the step's `env:`, next to `CLARIFY_SNAPSHOT_ALL_TEXT_ENABLED`. - After the `for attempt ... done` loop ends (about line 1800), add one block that runs once. It is not reached when the loop exits for the capacity wait (exit 0) or after all attempts fail (exit 1). New variables use the `clarify_bv_` prefix so they cannot clash with `rc`, `attempt` and the other loop variables. The block: - **Pick the helper.** Use `"${SUPPORT_SCRIPTS_DIR}/clarify_blocked_verify.sh"` only when `SUPPORT_SCRIPTS_DIR` is set and the file is a regular file that is not a symlink. Otherwise skip and log `CLARIFY_BLOCKED_VERIFY stage=verify outcome=skip reason=`, but only if the output has an unfenced `BLOCKED:` line (use a cheap grep for that). Never fall back to a `scripts/` copy in the checkout (see D3). - **Run `check`.** Use `|| clarify_bv_rc=$?`. On exit 0, run `prompt` to write `${RUNTIME_DIR}/codex_prompt_blocked_retry.txt` and copy `CODEX_OUTPUT_FILE` to `${RUNTIME_DIR}/codex_output_blocked_original.txt`. - **Make one engine call**, writing `${RUNTIME_DIR}/codex_output_blocked_retry.txt` and `${RUNTIME_DIR}/codex_log_blocked_retry.txt`. Use the same `CLARIFY_ENGINE` the loop finished with. The Claude path uses `_clarify_attempt_stderr_capture_start/stop`; exit code 75 switches to Codex for this call, as the loop does; exit code 80 counts as a failed retry. There is no backoff and no further attempts. - **On exit 0 with non-whitespace output,** copy the retry output over `CODEX_OUTPUT_FILE`. Log `CLARIFY_BLOCKED_VERIFY stage=retry outcome= exit_code=0`, where `still_blocked` means the retry output still has an unfenced `BLOCKED:` line. - **Otherwise,** leave `CODEX_OUTPUT_FILE` as it was (the original BLOCKED output) and log `stage=retry outcome=failed exit_code=`. - **The block never fails the step.** Every helper call carries `|| true` or captures its exit code. - The "Parse Codex output", "Handle blocked clarification output", semantic-cache and run-summary steps stay unchanged. They read `CODEX_OUTPUT_FILE`, so they see the retry result. A still-blocked or failed retry gives today's `ai:blocked` flow. 3. **Support staging.** - In `scripts/stage_support_for_phase.sh`, case `clarify)` (about line 100), change `stage_support_optional_scripts=(emit_event.sh)` to `stage_support_optional_scripts=(emit_event.sh clarify_blocked_verify.sh)`.
